recognitionNotes: Movie-only catalogue lookup is GET /?s={query}; candidates are selected from article links using title/year identity.
The old /movie/ fragment is not a search contract and must not be used as the executable entry route.
After the selected detail page, release/gateway URLs and form action targets are discovered dynamically from returned HTML; NiakVIO must not invent fixed paths for those steps.
Gateway resolution uses returned landing forms/redirects before DriveSeed/direct-media resolution; those dynamic targets remain stream traversal evidence rather than provider search-route DATA.
Search is a bounded GET catalogue lookup; selected watch entries resolve to /ep-{episode} pages.
data-video is an HTML player attribute and must never be emitted as an HTTP route.
Embed/player URLs are discovered from the selected episode page and require the provider origin as playback context when the stream host requires it.
Search rotates between NiakVIO-known worker origins and POSTs JSON to /1:search.
Episode searches use q, page_token and page_index; movie searches require q.
Player resolution may use a returned /download.aspx path or a returned worker path opened with a=view; the returned path itself remains DATA and is not guessed.
Existing durable NiakVIO player DATA is sufficient to classify this provider as routeful; no external repository lookup is required.
